page.layout: One column of running text, with a block of Syriac quotation in full lines below it. No margin notes, running head or catchword.

main_text.p: litate exaltationem, & paupertate diuitias, quamobrem intercede apud Christum Deum, vt saluet Animas nostras. En CANON. quo etiam adiuncto ornatur S. Nicolaus Episcopus Myrae, sub die 6. Decembris; sanctus Syluester Papa, sub die 2. Ianuarij; S. Leo Episcopus Catanensis, sub die 20. Februarij; sanctus Tharasius Archiepiscopus Constantinopolitanus, sub die 25. eiusdem. S. Porphyrius Episcopus Gazae, sub die 26. eiusdem; sanctus Nicephorus Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus, sub die secunda Iunij; S. Metrophanes Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus, sub die 4. eiusdem; sanctus Andreas Cretensis, sub die 4. Iulij. Eodem, & omnes fere sancti Patres. Garrit igitur ex more Hottingerus, & suos Reformatos, male cautos suis lactat mendacijs.
Ex Maronitis D. Ioannes Maro in præ-fatione Commentariorum ad Liturgiam sancti Iacobi, sic de Patrum iudicat do-ctrinam:

page.notes: The four lines at the foot are Syriac script, not Latin, Greek or Hebrew. I could not read them letter by letter at this scan resolution, so they are marked illegible; the letter counts are estimates. The printed page number 619 stands at the top right. No running head, catchword or signature is printed. The word "Christum" was read as Christum, and "Ioannes" was read from a small j-like form.
